title: One Time Frontend Control Tower Packet

reasons: GitHub issue #128 and the operator request ask for One Time full front-end product-quality work in parallel-safe audit mode first.
The work crosses public marketing, member/classroom, provider Operations, CRM/pipeline copy, helper, brand assets, and mobile routes, so it must be split.
The control tower shows a dirty worktree and active overlapping app-visible lane, so implementation must wait while audit/prompt/report work proceeds.
likely_external_provider_blockers: External sends, payments, checkout, access grants, DNS/Railway, Drive/Vimeo/Zoom, credentials, GHL, and LeadConnector are explicitly out of scope.
Operations screenshots require auth and redaction; missing auth blocks only the Operations audit slice.

operator_intent_summary: Make the One Time frontend feel like a high-trust, black/yellow, Rabbi Scheller product across public, member, classroom, and provider Operations surfaces, while preserving workspace scope and avoiding external/private mutations.
raw_quotes: Goal mode, but PARALLEL-SAFE AUDIT MODE FIRST.
Pick up GitHub issue #128 for the One Time frontend million-dollar app audit, static chrome, landing reframe, and Agent Mode prompt generation.
Do not implement shared app code if another lane is dirty or active in overlapping files.

decisions_captured.decision: Static chrome implementation is blocked by active dirty deploy lane until collision clears.
Countdown must be Israel-time and config/API-backed, not hardcoded in UI.
Drive mirror is optional; repo evidence is sufficient when Drive is unavailable.

out_of_scope: No email send, WhatsApp/WAPI send, Telegram send, Stripe checkout, charge, refund, access grant, password reset, DNS, Railway, Drive, Vimeo, Zoom, Resend, GHL, LeadConnector, credential, provider-account, or production-data mutation.

No screenshots, snapshots, logs, or reports containing raw private message bodies, student-sensitive details, secrets, passwords, API keys, payment card data, or unrelated provider/family records may be committed.
No app-visible implementation while the control tower shows an active dirty deploy lane in overlapping files.
No broad rewrite of BNA, Super Admin, parent, student, or provider shells beyond the packet scope.

inspection_targets: Control tower reports branch master with dirty worktree and overlapping active app-visible lanes.
GitHub issue #128 is open and contains owner decisions for countdown, $67 copy, first-party CRM/tracking, and scoped Rabbi Operations layout.
Existing One Time brand memory requires black/yellow and workspace isolation from BNA cream/navy/teal surfaces.
The new audit harness and Agent Mode prompts are safe audit/report artifacts and do not mutate external providers.
known_blockers: Active dirty deploy lane blocks static shared app implementation and commit/push/deploy closeout for this batch.
Authenticated Operations checks may be skipped or redacted when no safe session exists.

expanded_phrases.clean: Evidence-defined layout quality: no overlap, no clipped text, stable spacing, obvious hierarchy, and screenshot/readback proof by route and viewport.
expanded_phrases.nice: A route is acceptable only when it meets the same measurable visual, accessibility, and scope checks as the rest of the One Time surface.
expanded_phrases.ugly: Any inconsistent brand, broken layout, irrelevant data, or visibly untrusted placeholder becomes a coded visual finding with owner and next action.
expanded_phrases.sloppy: Sloppy means measurable defects: overflow, duplicate or misaligned controls, noisy setup/debug content, fake proof assets, wrong role data, or unsafe action copy.
expanded_phrases.million-dollar: A high-trust One Time product experience: black/yellow brand consistency, compact static chrome, clear first viewport, safe conversion flows, scoped role views, responsive controls, accessibility checks, screenshots, tests, and deploy/live-smoke gates for app-visible changes.
expanded_phrases.professional: Professional means role-appropriate information architecture, restrained but branded styling, aligned controls, predictable action states, and no private/admin/BNA bleed.
expanded_phrases.GHL-like: Use first-party BNA Operations patterns for CRM/pipeline concepts without GHL, LeadConnector, external CRM runtime, or provider mutation.
expanded_phrases.like GHL: Map CRM/pipeline expectations to first-party Operations views and registries only.
expanded_phrases.finish everything: Split the broad issue into packet-sized audited lanes with terminal statuses rather than a single broad implementation pass.
expanded_phrases.make it work: Define exact routes, action states, data reads, safe blockers, and verification commands before code changes.
expanded_phrases.community section: Classroom/community language is moderation-first and private-safe, never open student-to-student posting unless explicitly designed and authorized.
expanded_phrases.CRM: First-party One Time contact tracking and campaign status only; no GHL/LeadConnector runtime and no external CRM write.
expanded_phrases.pipeline: Pipeline means first-party status columns and task/action readbacks in scoped Operations, with safe preview states and no external mutation.
expanded_phrases.launch-ready: Launch-ready requires route registry/action registry coverage, screenshots, accessibility checks, no scope bleed, commit/push/deploy, and live smoke where app-visible.
expanded_phrases.configured: Configured means backed by explicit repo config/API readback and evidence, not a visual placeholder or unchecked claim.
expanded_phrases.working: Working means the user path has a successful readback or a precise blocker with owner and next action.

product_quality_expansion.first_party_pattern_interpretation: One Time CRM/pipeline and provider dashboard expectations map to first-party BNA Operations data and UI patterns only. GHL and LeadConnector are forbidden runtime dependencies.
